rule.name: Single Responsibility Principle
rule.statement: Every module, class, and function has exactly one reason to change.
rule.rationale: This codebase will be extended by multiple engines and adapters. Mixed responsibilities create hidden coupling that makes extension painful and breaks the open/closed principle.
rule.constraint: Each file in this project must map to exactly ONE of: data model, reader, writer, handler/orchestrator, utility, protocol/interface, adapter, or test. Never mix categories.
rule.example: # WRONG: context_builder.py merges tiers, enforces token budget, AND serializes def build_context(npc_id, player_msg): items = merge_tiers(...) # responsibility 1 items = trim_to_budget(...) # responsibility 2 return serialize(items) # responsibility 3

# RIGHT: three files, each with one job # context_merger.py → context_merger.merge(tier0, tier_a, tier_b) # token_budget_enforcer.py → enforce(items, budget) → trimmed items # context_serializer.py → serialize(items) → str # context_builder.py → thin facade chaining the three

rule.name: Open/Closed Principle
rule.statement: Modules are open for extension, closed for modification. New LLM backends, vector stores, distortion types, or emotion models must be addable by creating a new file, never by editing existing engine files.
rule.rationale: Engines and the gossip distortion system are expected to grow. If adding Mistral requires editing dialogue_handler.py, the design is wrong.
rule.constraint: All variable behavior must be behind a Protocol or abstract base class. Use factory functions to select implementations based on config. The factory is the only place that changes when a new implementation is added.
rule.example: # Adding a new LLM backend: # 1. Create engines/llm/openai_adapter.py implementing LLMClientProtocol # 2. Add "openai" case to engines/llm/factory.py # 3. No other file changes required

rule.name: Dependency Inversion Principle
rule.statement: High-level modules depend on abstractions (Protocols), not concrete implementations. Concrete dependencies are injected at the boundary (FastAPI dependency injection or constructor).
rule.rationale: Makes unit testing trivial: inject MockLLMClient without touching any engine code. Enables runtime swapping of Neo4j session, LLM backend, or vector store.
rule.constraint: No engine file may import a concrete adapter (mistral_adapter, neo4j driver, etc.) directly. Engines receive their dependencies as constructor arguments typed to the Protocol. FastAPI dependencies in api/dependencies.py are the composition root for the API layer.

rule.name: Interface Segregation Principle
rule.statement: Protocols must be small and focused. Do not add methods to a protocol that not all implementors will need. Split into multiple protocols if necessary.
rule.example: # LLMClientProtocol has generate, generate_structured, stream, model_name. # All adapters implement all four. If an adapter cannot stream, it raises # NotImplementedError — but streaming is architecturally required for WebSocket. # If a new adapter only generates text and has no structured output, create # a separate TextLLMClientProtocol and a StructuredLLMClientProtocol.

rule.name: Liskov Substitution Principle
rule.statement: Any class implementing a Protocol must be substitutable for any other implementation without changing program behavior. No implementation may weaken preconditions or strengthen postconditions relative to the Protocol's docstring.
rule.example: # WRONG: MockLLMClient.generate() returns "" for empty prompt, but real adapters raise # This breaks tests that test empty-prompt handling

rule.name: File Size Limit
rule.statement: No source file may exceed 200 lines (excluding blank lines and comments).
rule.rationale: Large files are a symptom of SRP violations. The 200-line limit forces extraction before files grow unwieldy. Docstrings and comments are excluded to encourage documentation.
rule.action_if_violated: Extract helpers to utils/, split readers/writers, or decompose the class. Never suppress the limit with a comment.

rule.name: Function Size Limit
rule.statement: No function or method may exceed 40 lines.
rule.rationale: Functions longer than 40 lines almost always contain multiple responsibilities or missing abstractions. Extract sub-functions with descriptive names.

rule.name: Module Docstrings
rule.statement: Every .py file must begin with a module-level docstring describing: 1. What this module does (one sentence) 2. What it does NOT do (scope boundary) 3. Key dependencies injected
rule.example:
""" relation_writer.py — Writes RELATES_TO edge mutations to Neo4j.
Does NOT open or commit transactions (graph_writer.py does that). Does NOT validate delta bounds (modifier_bounds_validator.py does that).
Dependencies: neo4j.AsyncSession (injected). """

rule.name: No Nesting Beyond 3 Levels
rule.statement: Control flow nesting (if/for/try) must not exceed 3 levels deep.
rule.action_if_violated: Extract inner blocks into named helper functions.

rule.name: No Magic Numbers or Strings
rule.statement: All constants must be named (ALL_CAPS module-level variable or config.py key). No raw numeric literals except 0 and 1 in logic. No raw string literals for node labels, relationship types, or config keys.
rule.example:
if trust > 50: # WRONG if trust > TRUST_NEUTRAL: # RIGHT (define TRUST_NEUTRAL = 50)
session.run("MATCH (c:Character)") # WRONG session.run(CYPHER_MATCH_CHARACTER) # RIGHT (define as constant)

rule.name: Immutability First
rule.statement: Never mutate an existing data structure in place. Always create and return a new object. Use Pydantic model_copy(update=...), dataclasses.replace(), or dict spreading.
rule.rationale: Mutation creates hidden side effects. The dialogue pipeline passes context through many steps; in-place mutation makes debugging pipeline state nearly impossible.

rule.name: Type Hints Everywhere
rule.statement: Every function parameter, return value, and class field must have a type annotation. No implicit Any. Use Optional[X] or X | None explicitly.

rule.name: Pydantic v2 for All Data Models
rule.statement: All data exchanged between layers (API schemas, graph nodes, engine inputs/outputs, config) must be Pydantic v2 BaseModel or BaseSettings. No raw dicts crossing module boundaries.
rule.rationale: Pydantic v2 gives free validation, serialization, and schema generation. Raw dicts allow silent type errors (wrong key name, wrong value type).
rule.example: def build_prompt(context: dict) -> str: # WRONG: opaque dict
def build_prompt(context: ContextSkeleton) -> str: # RIGHT: typed model

rule.name: Enums for Fixed Value Sets
rule.statement: Use Python Enum or Literal types for any field with a fixed set of valid values. Never use raw strings for action types, distortion types, knowledge states, etc.

rule.name: Protocols Over ABCs
rule.statement: Prefer typing.Protocol for interface definitions over abstract base classes. Protocols support structural subtyping (duck typing with type checker support), which works better with dependency injection and mocking.

rule.name: Fail Fast at System Boundaries
rule.statement: Validate all external inputs (API requests, LLM responses, Neo4j results, JSON file contents) immediately upon receipt. Raise or return error before passing invalid data inward.

rule.name: Custom Exception Hierarchy
rule.statement: All domain errors must be raised as typed custom exceptions defined in utils/errors.py. Never raise generic Exception or use bare except. Exception classes carry structured fields (not just a message string).
rule.example: raise GraphUnavailableError(uri=config.NEO4J_URI, cause=str(e)) raise LLMTimeoutError(model=self.llm.model_name(), timeout_s=config.LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) raise RelationDeltaExceededError(src=src_id, dst=dst_id, delta=delta, max_allowed=max_val)

rule.name: Never Silently Swallow Errors
rule.statement: Every except block must either re-raise, raise a domain error, log and re-raise, or return a typed error value. No bare except: pass.

rule.name: Resilience at Engine Boundaries
rule.statement: Each engine boundary (LLM call, Neo4j query) must have a defined fallback contract. LLM timeout → serve fallback_responses.json. Neo4j unavailable → raise GraphUnavailableError → API returns 503. Document the fallback in the function docstring.

rule.name: No Error Handling for Internal Invariants
rule.statement: Do not add try/except around code that calls internal functions you control. Internal invariants are enforced by type hints and Pydantic; catching them hides bugs. Only validate at system boundaries (API input, LLM output, DB results, file reads).

rule.name: Constructor Injection Only
rule.statement: All dependencies (DB session, LLM client, embedding index, config, stores) must be injected via __init__ constructor parameters. No global singletons accessed from inside engine or handler classes. No module-level instantiation of stateful objects.
rule.exception: config.py Settings instance may be a module-level singleton accessed via get_config() factory function. This is acceptable because Settings is immutable after startup.

rule.name: FastAPI Dependency Functions as Composition Root
rule.statement: api/dependencies.py is the only place where concrete implementations are instantiated and wired together. Route handlers receive dependencies via FastAPI Depends(). Route handlers must not instantiate anything directly.

rule.name: Inject Sessions, Never Open Them
rule.statement: Graph sub-writers (character_writer, relation_writer, etc.) receive an AsyncSession as a parameter. They never call driver.session() themselves. graph_writer.py is the only file that opens and commits transactions.

rule.name: Async All the Way Down
rule.statement: All I/O operations (Neo4j queries, LLM HTTP calls, embedding compute) must be async. Use async def and await. Never use blocking I/O in an async context. Use asyncio.gather() for independent parallel operations.

rule.name: Concurrency Cap on Batch Operations
rule.statement: asyncio.gather() calls that could spawn unbounded coroutines must use asyncio.Semaphore(config.MAX_CONCURRENT_TICKS) to cap concurrency.

rule.name: Thread-Safe Shared State
rule.statement: emotion_store and session_store hold in-memory state accessed concurrently. All mutations must be wrapped in asyncio.Lock(). Document the lock in the class docstring.

rule.name: Structured Logging
rule.statement: Use the structured logger from utils/logging.py. Never use print(). Log as key-value pairs: logger.info("event", npc_id=npc_id, tick=tick, ...). Include npc_id, player_id, tick, and duration_ms in all engine log entries.

rule.name: LLM Prompt Redaction in Production
rule.statement: LLM prompts and responses must only be logged when config.LOG_LLM_PROMPTS is True AND config.ENV == "dev". In staging and production, log only token counts and model name.
rule.rationale: NPC dialogue may contain player-sensitive content; do not log in production.

rule.name: RNG Seed Logging
rule.statement: All uses of random number generation (gossip pair selection, event sampling, distortion probability) must log the seed used at the start of each tick. This enables full reproducibility of any tick for debugging.

rule.name: Timing Instrumentation
rule.statement: Wrap all LLM calls and Neo4j queries with timing that emits duration_ms to the logger. This is the primary tool for identifying latency regressions before they affect players.

rule.name: Prompt Templates Are Versioned
rule.statement: All prompt templates live in docs/prompts.md with a version string (e.g., v1.2). The version must be included in LLM call logs. Never construct prompts by ad-hoc string concatenation inside engine code. prompt_builder.py is the only place that assembles prompts.

rule.name: Token Budget Enforcement
rule.statement: context_builder.py must enforce config.PROMPT_TOKEN_BUDGET before serialization. If budget is exceeded after Tier 0 + Tier A alone, raise TokenBudgetExceededError. Tier B (RAG) items are always optional; trim them first. Never pass an oversized context to the LLM silently.

rule.name: Structured Output Always Validated
rule.statement: LLM output from generate_structured() must be validated through a Pydantic model (response_parser.py) before any field is accessed. Never access LLM JSON fields directly with dict["key"].

rule.name: Few-Shot Examples Required
rule.statement: Stage B (realizer) prompt must include exactly two few-shot examples demonstrating the full output schema (npc_response, relation_deltas, mood_update, action, facial_expression). Examples are defined in docs/prompts.md and injected by prompt_builder.py.

rule.name: Idempotent Prompt Assembly
rule.statement: Given the same inputs (context skeleton, player message, session turns), prompt_builder.build_prompt() must return the exact same string every time. No timestamps or UUIDs injected into prompt content.
rule.rationale: Enables reliable prompt caching and reproducible debugging.

rule.name: Minimum 80% Coverage
rule.statement: All modules must maintain ≥ 80% line coverage measured by pytest-cov. CI will fail below this threshold.

rule.name: Pure Functions Are Fully Testable Without Mocks
rule.statement: gossip_distort(), token_budget_enforcer.enforce(), modifier_bounds_validator.clamp(), and context_serializer.serialize() are pure functions. Their tests must not use any mocks. If a mock is needed, the function is not pure.

rule.name: Integration Tests Use Real Neo4j
rule.statement: Integration tests for graph_writer.py must use a real Neo4j instance (testcontainers-python). No mocking the database in integration tests.
rule.rationale: Mock databases have historically masked schema mismatches and transaction edge cases.

rule.name: Mock LLM in All Non-LLM Tests
rule.statement: Any test that is not specifically testing an LLM adapter must use mock_adapter.py. No real LLM calls in unit or integration tests (cost + non-determinism).

rule.name: Test Error Paths Explicitly
rule.statement: Every error path (LLMTimeoutError, GraphUnavailableError, ValidationError, RelationDeltaExceededError) must have at least one test that triggers it and asserts the correct fallback behavior or HTTP status code.

rule.name: Every File Has a docs/files/ Entry
rule.statement: Before a file may be merged, a corresponding docs/files/<filename>.md must exist describing: purpose, public API (classes and functions), side effects, and an example.

rule.name: Docstring on Every Public Function
rule.statement: Every public function and class method must have a docstring with: - One-line summary - Args section (name: type — description) - Returns section - Raises section (if any exceptions are raised)

rule.name: ADRs for Non-Obvious Decisions
rule.statement: Any architectural decision with meaningful trade-offs must be documented in docs/adr/NNNN-title.md (Architecture Decision Record). Required for: choice of Neo4j over relational DB, WebSocket over SSE, in-memory emotion store, deterministic gossip distortion algorithm.

rule.name: No Secrets in Source Code
rule.statement: API keys, passwords, tokens, and seeds must only exist in environment variables. .env files must never be committed. .env.example with placeholder values is required.

rule.name: Parameterized Cypher Queries
rule.statement: All Neo4j Cypher queries must use parameterized form (e.g., {npc_id}). Never format user input directly into a Cypher string.

rule.name: Auth on All Non-Health Routes
rule.statement: Every route except GET /health must pass through auth/middleware.py. The middleware verifies the Authorization: Bearer {API_KEY_SECRET} header. Return HTTP 401 with no body detail on failure.

rule.name: Input Validation at API Boundary
rule.statement: All incoming request bodies are Pydantic models with field constraints. player_message must be capped at config.MAX_PLAYER_MESSAGE_CHARS (default 1000). delta_ticks in /clock/advance must be bounded [1, 1000]. Never pass unconstrained user input to Neo4j or LLM prompts.
